snippet.title: Daniel Radcliffe does not have advice for the next Harry Potter
snippet.description:
The old Harry Potter won’t be giving advice to the new Harry Potter, but he has a good reason.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry in the original film series, said he has “no advice” for Dominic McLaughlin, who takes over the role in HBO’s upcoming series. Radcliffe said he doesn’t want to “haunt this poor child” through interviews, with people saying, “Oh, and Dan said, you should do this.” He added that he’s “very excited” about the chance to meet him someday.

Asked whether he’ll watch the show, Radcliffe said, “I don’t know if I will, honestly.” He said he doesn’t watch any TV, and “eight hours is a lot of anything to watch.”

snippet.title: Daniel Radcliffe Predicts Some WILD Changes in a Harry Potter Remake!
snippet.description:
Daniel Radcliffe has a surprising choice for who he'd play in a future Harry Potter remake: Harry's father, James Potter! But he also has some concerns about how Hollywood approaches remakes.

Using Clash of the Titans as an example, Radcliffe questions why filmmakers sometimes change familiar details simply because they can, pointing to the traditionally white Pegasus being depicted as black in the remake. He then jokingly imagines the bizarre changes a new Harry Potter adaptation could make, including completely reinvented versions of Dumbledore and Hagrid!

snippet.description:

He also pointed out that there are plenty of classic TV shows he hasn’t even got around to watching yet, making the new Hogwarts series an unlikely addition to his watchlist.

snippet.title: Daniel Radcliffe's son has no idea his dad is Harry Potter. He just wants to be "Dad." 🥹✨
snippet.description:
In a world where Daniel Radcliffe is forever remembered as the boy wizard, there's one person who has no idea — his own three-year-old son[reference:0]. The 36-year-old actor, who became a global phenomenon as Harry Potter, is determined to keep that part of his life a secret for as long as possible[reference:1].

Radcliffe recently revealed in an interview with The New York Times that his son remains blissfully unaware of his father's fame[reference:2][reference:3]. He even conducted a subtle test: a DVD of the Harry Potter films sat on the kitchen table, and Radcliffe pointed to his younger self on the cover, asking, "Who's that?"[reference:4]. His son didn't recognize him[reference:5].

"For as long as I can just be his dad, and he won't know me as anything else, I will maintain that for as long as I can," Radcliffe said[reference:6][reference:7]. He cherishes this phase where he's simply "Dad" in his son's eyes, not a global movie star[reference:8].

Radcliffe prefers that when the time comes, his son watches the upcoming HBO Harry Potter series — a version without his dad on screen[reference:9]. "That'd be, honestly, the ideal," he explained[reference:10].

Would you keep a massive secret from your child just to be seen as "Dad" a little longer? 👇
